3.

As per the prosecution story, the lady alleged that she belonging to the Scheduled Caste category,
upon kidnapping of her minor daughter, presented an application before Hasanpur Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3584 of 2023(10) dt.05-02-2025 Police Station but the F.I.R. was not lodged, this happened on 18.10.2013.
Subsequently, on 15.12.2013, almost two months later, the Station Head Officer (henceforth for short 'the SHO') asked her to come to the Police Station and take the victim back to home.
4. Upon reaching there, she asked the SHO to let the boy take the daughter with him.

'The SHO'
thereafter also abused her and threw her out of the Police Station.
She later was informed by the victim that the appellant had taken her to Jaipur, (Rajasthan) and later returned to their native place which followed the recovery from the Police Station.

As the SHO, Hasanpur failed to register the F.I.R., she went to the 'Janta Darbar' which resulted into lodging of Mahila P.S. Case No. 31 of 2013 under different sections of the Indian Penal Code beside under the POCSO Act as the girl was minor.
5. The investigation took place in the matter and charge-sheet submitted against this appellant who was shown as an absconder on 21.05.2015.
Thereafter the cognizance was taken on 08.07.2015, the Trial went on separating the case of the appellant who subsequently surrendered on 21.11.2015 and remained in custody till 30.05.2016.

6. Once the appellant came into judicial custody, his Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.3584 of 2023(10) dt.05-02-2025 trial took place and after examination of witnesses and going through the facts, the Trial Court convicted and sentenced the appellant as follows:

Dilip Kumar R.I. for Rs. R.I. for six months.

 under Section 4 of  the POCSO  Act,

 R.I. for Rs. 5,000/- R.I. for one month  three years  under Section 363  of the  Indian  Penal Code  7.
Aggrieved the present appeal.
8. Earlier the coordinate Bench took up the matter and while admitting the appeal called for the Trial Court Record on 13.12.2023, which has now been received.

9. It is the case of the appellant that for a kidnapping of October 2013, F.I.R. came to be instituted in the month of December 2013 and a perusal of the F.I.R. would show that the lady wanted the girl to go along with appellant and only after his Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.3584 of 2023(10) dt.05-02-2025 refusal to do so
, he has been framed.
Earlier he remained in custody between 21.11.2015 to 30.05.2016 and later from his date of conviction on 22.05.2023, in that background, he deserves bail.

10. Mrs. Abha Singh representing the State on the other hand opposes the prayer submitting that the delay has been clearly explained by the lady that the SHO,
Hasanpur, Samastipur, chose not to register the F.I.R. and once the victim girl who was minor girl returned with the appellant, instead of putting him behind bar, the SHO wanted the informant to take the victim back.

Still despite request as no F.I.R.
was lodged, was forced lady to approach the 'Janta Darbar' which followed the F.I.R.
being registered with the Mahila Police Station.

11. It is her further submission that the girl being minor, the appellant having complete knowledge of it, took her away, remained for three months, returned and despite being presenting himself in the Police Station, the records shows that he remained absconder for almost two years, in that background, having not completed even half of his custody, bail may not be granted to him.
12. This Court has gone through the facts of the case and the materials on record as also the submissions of the Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.3584 of 2023(10)
dt.05-02-2025 parties and finds force in the submission of the learned APP
. The conduct of the appellant as also the then SHO, Hasanpur, Samastipur clearly show that both were hand in glove.
A minor girl was missing, the helpless mother was moving from one place to other, approached the Police Station who chose to look the other way.

Worse, once the girl returned, instead of putting the appellant behind bar,
he was let free which resulted into he having absconded for two years despite lodging of the F.I.R.

sentences.text: The then S.H.O. Hasanpur had lot to explain but since lots of water has flown down the ganges in last one decade, this Court rests the case.

13. In that background, when the Trial Court has finally convicted him and the maximum punishment given is 7 years, he having not completed even half of the judicial custody, for the present, no relief can be granted to the appellant.
14. Accordingly, the prayer for bail stands rejected.

(Rajiv Roy, J) vinayak/-
